This is equivalent to finding a 3-coloring of {1, ..., 38} without a monochromatic AP of length 3. By definition, the Van der Waerden number W(3, 3) is the smallest integer n such that any 3-coloring of {1, ..., n} contains a monochromatic AP of length 3. It is a well-known result that W(3, 3) = 27. Since 38 >= 27, it is impossible to color the integers 1 to 38 with 3 colors without creating a monochromatic AP of length 3. Therefore, the problem is unsatisfiable.
